findings.summary: The stray-field figure is laid out on a 15 x 5.8 in canvas (figure.py:177) but save() rewrites every SVG's width and height to 31.1111cm x 16cm, which is the 14 x 7.2 slide ratio. The rendered PNG therefore letterboxes: its 541 px are only 407 px of content (rows 67-473), the rest is empty transparent margin above and below, so a quarter of the figure's height is spent on nothing and the three panels are sized for a canvas they no longer match.

The permeability contours are stroked at linewidths=0.8, about 1.1 px in the 1400 px render and below the 2.6 pt data-series weight the house style sets. At the roughly 900 px column width the loops thin to sub-pixel hairlines, and the top level is viridis yellow-green (about #90d743, roughly 1.7:1 on white), so the highest-permeability contour is the least visible line in the figure.

The 'above the arms' panel draws four upper and four lower curves per model in the same two colours, with no marker, dash or direct label tying a curve to its Z or to upper versus lower, and the curves cross between R about 1.2 and 2.4 m. A reader can see that stored and true differ but cannot attribute any curve to a probe row, so the panel does not deliver the per-Z reading its name promises.
